reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins with the alignment of mental cleavages—how cognition partitions reality—into natural categories. This alignment enables philosophy to organize empirical data according to cognitive schemas. When such alignment succeeds, moral and aesthetic relations become applicable to real-world entities rather than mere mental constructs. A priori truths emerge as necessary conditions for this alignment, expressing comparisons among mental terms. These truths gain empirical relevance when nature behaves as though its realities mirror these mental terms. The rational intelligibility postulate asserts that the world’s structure conforms to an ideal logical system, enabling consistent formalization. Failure occurs when mental models do not reflect natural structure, leading to disconnected moral/aesthetic principles and failed predictions.
